correctness.rationale: Taking logs of the factorial likelihood ratio gives the stated deterministic correction; its difference from lambda_n is O(n^3/K^2). Uniform approximation by continuous-density cell averages gives K s_2 -> integral f^2, and boundedness gives s_h=O(K^(1-h)). For occupancy b at most 2 the log numerator is exactly log(2) times the pair count; for b>=3 the discrepancy is bounded by a constant times binom(b,3) and the expected triple count is O(lambda_n n/K). At the critical scale the disjoint ordered pairs have count (n)_{2r}/2^r; every overlapping factorial-moment graph has v>=2c+1 and contributes O(n^(2c-v)), so the factorial moments converge to those of the moment-determinate Poisson law. When lambda_n grows, independence of disjoint pairs and the joint probability s_3 for two pairs sharing one index give the displayed variance (three unordered pair-pairs on each index triple); this is o(lambda_n^2). When lambda_n tends to zero use Markov on the pair count. Integrating the cosine cell-wise gives the sinc-squared attenuation of the cosine amplitude; the grid mean of the cosine is zero and of its square is 1/2 for d>=3 (not d=2), yielding the exact stated energy and cutoff. A separately written bounded test passed 1808 checks of the finite likelihood-ratio identity, unit null mean, pair moments and grid energy; these do not establish any limiting assertions. The null transfer is via Henzi–Law's Proposition 1(iii), while the alternative, unscaled cutoff equality, and any grid-changing sequential interpretation are explicitly delimited in the frozen theorem.

evidence: Henzi–Law §3.3 Theorem 2 assumes 40 d sqrt(log N) <= sqrt(N)/e and gives a KL-dependent bound for rejection by time N. This excludes d much larger than sqrt(N), as required here. Section 3.4 compares mixtures of grids, not the terminal triangular array.

The Stanford Bayesian birthday calculation studies the probability of any match under a random Dirichlet law, and compares it to iid uniform draws. It gives the exponent with the doubled collision intensity under the prior predictive for a zero-collision event, not the sign of log evidence under a fixed nonuniform f.

The many-collision range allows triples to be frequent in absolute number, so neglecting them requires the relative triple bound. Converting the collision LLN into log evidence compares a pair reward log(2) times the cell energy against a deterministic cost of 1 per unit lambda_n.

The same-paper null rank statement is a direct substitution and is not assessed as a new rank theorem.

evidence: The statistic is the ratio of the symmetric Dirichlet-one integrated multinomial probability to the uniform multinomial probability; Henzi–Law equations (9)–(11) state the exact identity. The common multinomial coefficient cancels if written for counts instead of sequences.

value.rationale: Identifies a non-Gaussian terminal calibration exactly where collision noise first survives. More importantly, it quantifies a real grid-resolution failure mode for this particular evidence functional: even positive analytic dependent oracle copulas can yield vanishing terminal evidence, with the precise energy at which that reverses. This is useful for comparing evidence procedures and interpreting a fine grid, without making power claims about empirical sequential ranks.
